units.title: Heredity and Evolution
units.origin: Mendel's pea laws (1866, rediscovered 1900); chromosome theory by Sutton & Boveri (1902–03); DNA structure by Watson, Crick, Franklin & Wilkins (1953).
units.discovered: Double helix 1953; genetic code cracked 1961–66 (Nirenberg, Khorana); Human Genome Project 1990–2003.
units.mechanism: Genes on chromosomes segregate and assort into gametes; DNA replicates semiconservatively, transcribes to mRNA and translates to protein under regulated switches; mutation plus selection shifts populations (Hardy–Weinberg baseline), radiating adaptations — including humans.
features: Mendel's dominance, segregation, independent assortment — with extensions (incomplete dominance, linkage)
Chromosome theory marries Mendel to meiosis
Central dogma: DNA → RNA → protein, regulated per cell type
Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium as the no-evolution null model
properties: Genotype hidden, phenotype shown; test crosses reveal carriers
Linkage breaks Mendel's ratios; crossing over rescues variation
Sex-linked traits follow X/Y transmission rules
DNA constancy across species contrasts with endless sequence variety
units.details: Monohybrid (3:1) and dihybrid (9:3:3:1) crosses anchor inheritance; codominance and linkage complicate it. Sex determination (XX/XY) explains haemophilia and colour-blindness patterns. Molecularly, Watson–Crick DNA unwinds, copies, and expresses through transcription–translation with operon-level regulation. The Human Genome Project (3 billion bases, ~20,000 genes) turned medicine predictive; Hardy–Weinberg maths plus fossil/DNA evidence close the loop to human evolution.

topics.title: Mendel's laws of inheritance — monohybrid and dihybrid cross
topics.origin: Mendel, Experiments on Plant Hybrids (1866); ignored until 1900.
topics.mechanism: Allele pairs separate into gametes (segregation); different genes assort independently — Punnett squares predict the ratios.
keyPoints: Pea-trait logic applied to human pedigrees

topics.title: Incomplete dominance and codominance
topics.origin: Correns documented blending inheritance (1900s); ABO codominance (Landsteiner, 1900).
topics.mechanism: Heterozygotes show intermediate (pink snapdragon) or dual (AB blood) phenotypes because neither allele fully masks the other.
keyPoints: Roan cattle and sickle-cell heterozygote edge

topics.title: Linkage and crossing over
topics.origin: Morgan's fly room (1910s); Creighton & McClintock proved crossing over physically (1931).
topics.mechanism: Genes on one chromosome travel together (parental combos dominate) until meiotic crossovers swap segments, scrambling them.
keyPoints: Gene maps built from test-cross data

topics.title: Sex determination and sex-linked disorders
topics.mechanism: XX/XY (or ZW) sets sex; X-linked recessives strike hemizygous males most, passing criss-cross from mother to son.

topics.title: Chromosome theory of inheritance
topics.origin: Sutton & Boveri (1902–03), confirmed by Morgan's flies.
topics.mechanism: Chromosomes behave exactly like Mendel's factors — pairing, segregating and assorting in meiosis — because they ARE the factors' vehicles.

topics.title: Molecular basis of inheritance: DNA, replication, transcription, translation, regulation
topics.mechanism: Helicase unzips, polymerase copies semiconservatively; RNA polymerase transcribes genes; ribosomes translate codons to amino acids; repressors/operators switch operons.

topics.title: Human Genome Project — objectives and significance
topics.mechanism: Shotgun + clone sequencing read all 3 billion bases, mapped ~20,000 genes, and opened predictive, preventative medicine.
keyPoints: Goals: sequence, map variation (SNPs), share data

topics.title: Evolution: evidences, adaptive radiation, Hardy–Weinberg, human evolution
topics.origin: Modern synthesis (1930s–40s); Hardy–Weinberg (1908); Pääbo's ancient DNA (Nobel 2022).
topics.mechanism: Fossils, embryos and DNA prove descent; empty niches radiate forms (finches, mammals); allele maths (p²+2pq+q²) detects selection; hominins walked the bipedal branch.
keyPoints: Human ascent recap from anthropoid stock

units.title: Human Health and Diseases
units.origin: Germ theory (Pasteur/Koch, 1860s–80s); antibodies by von Behring (1890, Nobel 1901); vaccines from Jenner (1796).
units.discovered: Penicillin 1928 (Fleming); HIV identified 1983; immune network theory and clonal selection (Burnet, 1950s).
units.mechanism: Pathogens invade via air, water, vectors and contact; innate barriers and phagocytes strike first, then B/T lymphocytes mount specific antibody and killer-cell responses with memory — vaccines pre-train that memory without the disease.
features: Ten-disease dossier: malaria to ringworm — agent, spread, symptoms, control
Innate (skin, interferon, complement) vs adaptive (humoral + cellular)
Antigen–antibody lock-and-key with memory cells
Allergy (overreaction) vs autoimmunity (self-attack) vs AIDS (defence collapse)
properties: Vaccination: live-attenuated, killed, subunit, mRNA platforms
Antibiotics hit bacteria only — useless on viruses
Sanitation + vectors + drugs = the control triangle
units.details: Each pathogen gets its profile — Plasmodium (mosquito), dengue virus (Aedes), Wuchereria, Ascaris, pneumonia bacteria, Salmonella typhi, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, rhinovirus, HIV, ringworm fungus. Immunity chapters layer physical barriers, inflammation, interferons, then lymphocyte specificity, MHC presentation and memory. Vaccination schedules, allergy mediators (histamine/IgE) and autoimmune examples (rheumatoid arthritis) plus AIDS management complete the unit.

topics.title: Pathogens and diseases: malaria, dengue, filariasis, ascariasis, pneumonia, typhoid, TB, cold, AIDS, ringworm
topics.origin: Each agent isolated between 1880s (typhoid, TB) and 1980s (HIV).
topics.mechanism: Vector bite, droplet, faecal–oral or contact delivers the agent; it multiplies, damages tissue and exits to the next host.

topics.title: Immune system — innate and adaptive immunity
topics.origin: Metchnikoff (phagocytosis) vs Ehrlich (antibodies), Nobel 1908; lymphocyte roles (1960s).
topics.mechanism: Skin, mucus, acid, interferon and complement blunt invasion within hours; lymphocytes then learn the invader and remember it for years.

topics.title: Antigens and antibodies, immune response
topics.mechanism: Epitopes trigger clonal B/T expansion; plasma cells flood Ig while killers lyse infected cells; memory cells await round two.

topics.title: Vaccination and immunization
topics.mechanism: Harmless antigen trains memory without disease; boosters refresh it; herd coverage starves outbreaks.
keyPoints: Live, killed, subunit, toxoid, mRNA types

topics.title: Allergy and autoimmune diseases
topics.mechanism: IgE–histamine misfires on pollen/dust; regulatory failures let lymphocytes attack joints, myelin or islets instead.
keyPoints: Rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, type-1 diabetes examples
AIDS contrast: defence collapse, not misfire

units.title: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
units.origin: Green Revolution (Borlaug, 1940s–60s, Nobel 1970); single-cell protein concept (1960s); white/blue revolutions for milk and fish.
units.discovered: Dwarf wheat/rice varieties 1960s; Bt crops 1990s; biofortified crops 2000s+.
units.mechanism: Breeders cross, select and hybridise for yield and resistance; microbes and algae become protein (SCP); elite livestock breeds plus feed/health management multiply milk, meat and eggs; biofertilisers feed soil instead of poisoning it.
features: Plant breeding pipeline: collection → evaluation → crossing → selection → release
SCP: Spirulina, yeast, Fusarium protein vats
Animal husbandry: indigenous + exotic breeds, MOET, artificial insemination
Biofertilisers: Rhizobium, Azolla, mycorrhiza, cyanobacteria
properties: Nepal angle: terrace crops, buffalo, carp polyculture
units.details: Mass/pure-line/mutation breeding and hybridisation build resilient varieties (with Green Revolution history as caution and triumph). SCP turns petroleum, molasses or sunlight into protein. Dairy/poultry/fishery management — housing, feed formulation, vaccination — scales output. Biofertilisers close the nutrient loop for sustainable agriculture.

topics.title: Plant breeding — methods and examples
topics.origin: Vavilov's centres of origin (1920s); Borlaug's dwarf wheat (1960s).
topics.mechanism: Cross contrasting parents, select segregants over generations, multiply the winner — mutation and polyploidy add raw novelty.

topics.title: Single cell protein (SCP)
topics.mechanism: Fast microbes convert cheap substrates into protein-rich biomass harvested, dried and eaten or fed.
keyPoints: Protein content rivals meat per gram

topics.title: Animal husbandry — breeds and management
topics.origin: Operation Flood/white revolution (1970s); AI technique (20th century).
topics.mechanism: Elite genetics × nutrition × health management multiply milk, meat, eggs and fish; AI and MOET spread winners fast.
keyPoints: Dairy, poultry, fishery snapshots for Nepal

topics.title: Biofertilizers and sustainable agriculture
topics.mechanism: Nitrogen-fixers and P-solubilisers feed crops biologically; rotations, compost and IPM keep soil alive.
keyPoints: Urea vs biology: cost and soil comparison

units.title: Microbes in Human Welfare
units.origin: Fermentation science (Pasteur, 1857); antibiotics (Fleming 1928, Florey/Chain 1940s); biogas engineering (20th century).
units.discovered: Citric-acid fermentation (1917, Currie); Bt biopesticide (1960s); oil-spill bioremediation (1980s+).
units.mechanism: Yeast respire sugar to alcohol/CO₂; Penicillium secretes antibiotics; Aspergillus excretes citric acid; Bacillus/Baculoviruses kill pests selectively; methanogens digest waste to biogas while others eat oil and metals.
features: Household trio: curd (LAB), bread (yeast), cheese (moulds + bacteria)
Industrial trio: penicillin, ethanol, citric acid
Biocontrol: Bt toxin, NPV viruses, Trichoderma fungi
Cleanup crew: oil-eaters, metal-leachers, biogas digesters
units.details: Household fermentation (Lactobacillus curd, Saccharomyces dough, Propionibacterium cheese holes) scales to antibiotic tanks, distillery vats and citric-acid fermenters. Bt cotton's Cry protein and viral/fungal biocontrol replace broad pesticides. Bioremediation (Pseudomonas oil spills), biomining and gobar-gas plants turn pollution into product.

topics.title: Microorganisms in household products
topics.mechanism: Lactic-acid bacteria sour milk to curd; yeast leavens dough with CO₂; ripening cultures flavour cheese.

topics.title: Industrial production: antibiotics, beverages, citric acid
topics.mechanism: Aerated sterile tanks grow producers; downstream extraction purifies the molecule.

topics.title: Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers
topics.mechanism: Cry toxins, viral infections and fungal parasites kill pests selectively; fixers and solubilisers feed plants.

topics.title: Bioremediation and biogas
topics.origin: Exxon Valdez bioremediation (1989) proved the cleanup; gobar plants (20th century).
topics.mechanism: Oil-eating bacteria mineralise spills; methanogen consortia digest dung to methane in sealed digesters.
keyPoints: Gobar-gas plant design and slurry value

units.title: Biotechnology — Principles and Processes
units.origin: Recombinant DNA: Cohen–Boyer (1973); PCR: Mullis (1983, Nobel 1993); sequencing: Sanger (1977).
units.discovered: Restriction enzymes (1970s, Nobel 1978); Ti plasmid vectors; gel electrophoresis routine by 1980s.
units.mechanism: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at palindromes; ligase pastes foreign genes into plasmid/λ vectors; competent hosts (CaCl₂/heat-shock or electroporation) take them up; PCR then photocopies any target billions-fold while electrophoresis sorts fragments by size.
features: Core premise: alien DNA replicates inside a living host
Tool trinity: enzymes, vectors, competent host
Process chain: isolate → cut → ligate → transfer → select → culture
Downstream analytics: PCR + blots + sequencing
properties: Selectable markers (ampR, lacZ) find the winners
PCR needs primers, Taq, and thermal cycling
units.details: Principles chapters justify rDNA (universal genetic code, replicon autonomy). Tools chapters profile EcoRI-style enzymes, pBR322/Ti/viral vectors and Agrobacterium's natural engineering. Process chapters walk DNA isolation (lysis → RNase/protease → precipitation), PCR cycles (denature–anneal–extend), agarose gels, Southern blotting and gene-gun/microinjection transfer — ending in bioreactors.

topics.title: Principles of biotechnology — recombinant DNA technology
topics.mechanism: Universal code + autonomous replicons let any gene work in any host — cut, paste, copy, express.
keyPoints: Why alien genes work anywhere (shared code)

topics.title: Tools: restriction enzymes, vectors, competent host
topics.mechanism: Palindromic cutters open DNA; vectors carry inserts past selection; porous hosts admit them.
keyPoints: Sticky vs blunt ends; EcoRI exemplar

topics.title: Processes: DNA isolation, PCR, gel electrophoresis, gene transfer
topics.mechanism: Extract pure DNA, amplify the target region, visualise bands, deliver constructs into cells/plants/animals.

topics.title: Applications of recombinant DNA technology
topics.mechanism: Same toolbox yields drugs, diagnostics, engineered crops and research models.

units.title: Biotechnology and Its Applications
units.origin: Bt crops (1990s); Humulin (1982); Dolly the clone (1996); CRISPR era (2012+).
units.discovered: Agrobacterium Ti mechanism (1970s); gene-therapy trials (1990s); Bt brinjal debates (2000s).
units.mechanism: Cry genes make crops their own pesticide; nematode-resistance silences pest genes by RNAi; human insulin, growth hormone and clotting factors pour from vats; corrected genes ride vectors into patients; transgenic animals model disease — while biopiracy fights decide who owns life.
features: Agri wins: Bt cotton (bollworm-proof), RNAi tobacco (nematode-proof)
Medicine wins: insulin, interferon, tPA, gene therapy for ADA–SCID
Animal wins: transgenic mice, pharming goats, salmon
Controversy wins: patents, terminator fears, biopiracy cases
units.details: Agriculture chapters detail Cry endotoxin mode-of-action and RNA-interference nematode control with yield data. Medicine chapters follow insulin from pig extracts to Humulin vats, plus gene-therapy vectors and therapeutic proteins. Transgenic-animal chapters weigh pharming promise against welfare. Closing chapters litigate biopiracy (neem, basmati, turmeric cases) and patent regimes.

topics.title: Agriculture: Bt cotton, nematode-resistant tobacco
topics.origin: Bt spray (1960s) → Bt genes in plants (1990s); RNAi mechanism (Fire/Mello, Nobel 2006).
topics.mechanism: Cry crystals perforate bollworm guts; host-delivered dsRNA silences nematode parasitism genes.
keyPoints: Cry protein activation inside insect gut

topics.title: Medicine: insulin, gene therapy, therapeutic proteins
topics.mechanism: Vats express human proteins; AAV/retroviral vectors deliver fixed genes to patient cells.

topics.title: Transgenic animals
topics.mechanism: Pronuclear injection or ES-cell targeting inserts genes; herds then secrete drugs in milk or model human disease.

topics.title: Biopiracy and patent issues
topics.mechanism: Traditional knowledge gets patented abroad; challenges cite prior art; treaties now demand consent and sharing.
keyPoints: What patent offices allow on life

units.title: Organisms and Environment
units.origin: Population ecology (Malthus 1798 → Verhulst 1838 logistic → Lotka–Volterra 1920s); ecosystem energetics (Odum, 1950s).
units.mechanism: Organisms tolerate only bands of temperature, water and salts (acclimatise, migrate or die); populations grow exponentially until competition, predation and disease bend them into S-curves at K; ecosystems meanwhile fix, move and release carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus while succession reweaves disturbed ground.
features: Adaptation toolbox: conform, regulate, migrate, suspend
Population traits: natality, mortality, age pyramids, growth forms
Interactions: competition, predation, parasitism, commensalism, mutualism
Ecosystem services: productivity, decomposition, succession, cycling
properties: Liebig's minimum + Shelford's tolerance set limits
J vs S curves diagnose resource states
Decomposition rate hinges on chemistry + climate
Pioneer → climax succession is directional but not destiny
units.details: Adaptation chapters sort regulators vs conformers with hibernation/aestivation/migration exits. Population chapters quantify growth (exponential vs logistic maths), age-structure pyramids and Lotka–Volterra duels. Ecosystem chapters audit pond/forest productivity, detritus vs grazing chains, decomposition steps and hydrarch/xerarch succession — with full C/N/P cycle accounting and pyramid/energy-flow diagrams.

topics.title: Adaptations of organisms to environmental conditions
topics.origin: Malthus (1798) warned; Darwin (1859) explained; tolerance law (Shelford, 1913).
topics.mechanism: Regulators hold internal constancy, conformers track the environment, migrants leave and suspenders sleep through hardship.

topics.title: Population ecology — growth, regulation, interactions
topics.mechanism: Births minus deaths steer numbers toward K; competition, predation and cooperation tune the trajectory.

topics.title: Ecosystem structure and function — productivity, decomposition
topics.origin: Odum's Silver Springs study (1957) balanced an ecosystem's books.
topics.mechanism: GPP minus respiration funds all consumers; detritivores shred, leach, fragment and mineralise litter back to producers.

topics.title: Ecological succession
topics.origin: Dune studies (Cowles, 1899); Clements vs Gleason debate (1916–26).
topics.mechanism: Pioneers trap soil and water, mid-seral species shade them out, and a self-replacing climax settles — hydrarch in water, xerarch on rock.

topics.title: Nutrient cycling — carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus
topics.origin: Cycle chemistry from Lavoisier to Redfield (1934 ocean ratio).
topics.mechanism: Photosynthesis–respiration shuttles carbon; fixers–nitrifiers–denitrifiers shuttle nitrogen; weathering shuttles phosphorus.

topics.title: Ecological pyramids and energy flow
topics.mechanism: Each transfer burns ~90%, so pyramids narrow and chains stay short — energy flows one way while matter cycles.

units.title: Biodiversity and Conservation
units.origin: Biodiversity coined by Rosen (1985); hotspots by Myers (1988); CBD (1992).
units.discovered: Red Data Book (1966); Nepal community-forestry success (1990s+).
units.mechanism: Count diversity at gene, species and ecosystem levels; map where it concentrates (tropics, Nepal's Himalaya) and why it bleeds (habitat, overuse, invasion, pollution, climate); then defend in place (parks, corridors) and in backup (banks, gardens, Red-List triage).
features: Three biodiversity levels with measurement tricks
Global patterns: latitudinal gradient, species–area curves
Loss drivers with Nepalese examples
In-situ + ex-situ + law + Red Data Book toolkit
units.details: Biodiversity chapters quantify richness, evenness and endemism, then walk global and Nepal patterns (Terai–Himalaya transects). Loss chapters autopsy habitat conversion, poaching, invasives, pollution and warming. Conservation chapters design reserves (SLOSS, corridors), run ex-situ backup, enforce CITES/national law and read Red Data Book accounts.

topics.title: Biodiversity — genetic, species, ecosystem levels
topics.origin: Rosen (1985) gave the crisis its name.
topics.mechanism: Allele variety buffers populations, species variety buffers ecosystems, habitat variety buffers regions — measure each to manage each.
keyPoints: Richness vs evenness vs endemism metrics

topics.title: Patterns of biodiversity — global and Nepal
topics.mechanism: Energy, area and history pile species toward the tropics; Nepal's altitude transect compresses many biomes into one country.

topics.title: Biodiversity loss — causes and consequences
topics.mechanism: HIPPO drivers shrink and split populations until chance finishes them; services (pollination, water, genes) fail with them.

topics.title: Conservation strategies — in-situ and ex-situ
topics.mechanism: Protect, connect, breed, bank and legislate — matching each threat with its countermeasure.

topics.title: Red Data Book and IUCN categories
topics.mechanism: Population size, decline rate and range thresholds sort species into threat bands that trigger action and funding.

units.title: Environmental Issues
units.origin: Greenhouse physics (Fourier 1824, Tyndall 1859, Arrhenius 1896); ozone hole (Farman et al., 1985); waste science (20th century).
units.discovered: Keeling curve (1958+); Montreal Protocol (1987); Paris Agreement (2015).
units.mechanism: Fossil smoke and dust choke air; sewage and effluents starve water of oxygen; plastics and e-waste pile on land; radiation damages genes; CO₂/CH₄ trap heat, CFCs eat ozone — controls run from scrubbers and STPs to segregation, treaties and rainwater harvesting.
features: Air: smog, SPM, SO₂/NOₓ, indoor smoke
Water: BOD, eutrophication, heavy metals, pathogens
Land/radiation: solid, biomedical, e-waste; nuclear hazards
Global trio: warming, ozone loss, plus local fixes (harvest, wasteland greening)
properties: Mitigation hierarchy: avoid → reduce → reuse → treat
units.details: Air chapters source apportion (vehicles, brick kilns, cooking smoke) and prescribe filters, fuel switching and standards. Water chapters trace sewage/industrial paths through DO crashes to STP/ETP treatment trains. Waste chapters sort municipal, biomedical and e-waste into 4R handling; radiation chapters cover sources, units and shielding. Climate chapters explain greenhouse physics, ozone chemistry (CFC → Cl → O₃ loss), then land solutions: rainwater harvesting structures and wasteland afforestation.

topics.title: Air pollution — causes, effects, control
topics.origin: London smog deaths (1952) launched clean-air law worldwide.
topics.mechanism: Combustion and dust emit gases/particles that inflame lungs, cut visibility and seed acid rain.

topics.title: Water pollution — causes, effects, control
topics.mechanism: Sewage and effluents rot in rivers, crashing dissolved oxygen; nutrients trigger blooms; metals and pathogens persist.
keyPoints: STP/ETP trains and river action plans

topics.title: Solid waste management
topics.mechanism: Segregated waste composts, recycles or energy-recovers; only inert residue landfills safely.

topics.title: Nuclear radiation hazards
topics.mechanism: Ionising rays break DNA — dose × time decides harm; distance, shielding and containment cut exposure.

topics.title: Greenhouse effect, global warming, climate change
topics.origin: Arrhenius (1896) computed CO₂ warming; Keeling measured it (1958+).
topics.mechanism: IR-absorbing gases blanket Earth; extra CO₂/CH₄ thicken the blanket — glaciers, monsoons and seas respond.
keyPoints: Impacts on Nepal: floods, drought, disease

topics.title: Ozone layer depletion
topics.mechanism: CFC chlorine cycles shred stratospheric ozone catalytically; the Montreal Protocol phased CFCs out.
keyPoints: Cl + O₃ → ClO + O₂ catalytic loop
Montreal as the treaty that worked

topics.title: Rainwater harvesting and wasteland development
topics.mechanism: Catchments, recharge pits and check dams bank monsoon water; hardy plantations reclaim degraded commons.
